why_ai: Unlicensed screen work turning others' markups into sheets, which AI documentation and detailing automation increasingly generate directly.
why_clarity: Drawing standards and detailing codes define a checkable deliverable, though errors surface weeks later at review or erection.
why_digital: Markups and models in, drawing sets out, bought remotely with offshore bureaus the norm.

why_ai: Connection fit-up and design-conflict judgement plus fabricator trust protect it partly, but modelling and connections automate.
why_clarity: AISC practice and piece-level fit give objective checks, with field-fix feedback arriving at erection.
why_digital: Design drawings in, models and shop drawings out, bought by fabricators from onshore and offshore detailers.

why_ai: Production of sheets from a firm's markups is the hours AI documentation tools are built to remove.
why_clarity: Sheet sets against markups and standards are checkable, and the work recurs across projects.
why_digital: Models, DWGs and PDFs in and out, sourced remotely worldwide.

why_ai: One-off per-sheet production is a commodity bought on price and the most exposed to generated drawings.
why_clarity: Marked-up sets to finished sheets is a defined, highly repetitive task with quick client acceptance.
why_digital: Entirely remote, often brokered through online marketplaces.

why_ai: Continuity of a known team gives some relationship value, but the production itself automates.
why_clarity: Work is repetitive inside one firm's standards, though quality is argued rather than measured.
why_digital: Remote access to the client's own systems from offshore delivery centres.

why_ai: Site measurement and local plan-check knowledge protect a share of the work from remote or automated drafting.
why_clarity: Approval by the building department is a clear test, but local habits vary and are learned by experience.
why_digital: Starts with site visits and sketches, drawn on screen, bought locally from known drafters.

why_ai: Raster-to-vector conversion and text recognition are squarely in the path of computer vision.
why_clarity: Converting a sheet faithfully is exact and repetitive, with dimensional checks available.
why_digital: Paper archives in, CAD out, conversion commonly sent offshore.

why_ai: Reading specifications, architect intent and field conditions keeps judgement in the loop for small trades.
why_clarity: First-submittal approval is a clear target, but each project's specifications and comments vary.
why_digital: Drawings are digital, inputs include field dimensions, and trades buy from known bureaus.

why_ai: Rule-bound line drawings from CAD and photos are among the most automatable drafting tasks.
why_clarity: 37 CFR 1.84 gives an exact, checkable standard on highly repetitive figures.
why_digital: Sketches and CAD in, PDF figures out, bought remotely from bureaus worldwide.

why_ai: Spooling and routing rules automate, but first-time field fit depends on installer and shop judgement.
why_clarity: LOD 400 spools fit or they do not, recurring floor by floor with fast feedback.
why_digital: Models in, spool data out to physical prefabrication, modelled remotely for contractors.

why_ai: Bar shapes, laps and lists follow codified rules that generators can apply from structural drawings.
why_clarity: ACI and CRSI rules make placing drawings exact, repetitive and quickly checked against shipments.
why_digital: Structural drawings in, bar lists out to fabricators, often detailed offshore.

why_ai: A licensed engineer must seal delegated connection design and carries the liability for it.
why_clarity: Connection checks follow AISC provisions with objective calculations, reviewed within the approval window.
why_digital: Forces and drawings in, sealed calculations out, bought nationally by fabricators.

why_ai: Product-bundled detailing under engineering responsibility, with design and drawings increasingly generated.
why_clarity: Standard products detailed to codified rules at high volume with clear approval outcomes.
why_digital: Orders in, drawings out with physical product, sold through manufacturer sales channels.

why_ai: Coordinating vendors, revisions and back-charges against shop and site realities takes accountable judgement.
why_clarity: Package status is clear, but back-charge attribution is argued case by case.
why_digital: Digital packages and schedules, with shop-floor and site inputs.

why_ai: Rule-bound placing drawings and bar lists are automatable, though bundled with physical supply.
why_clarity: Codified rebar rules make the output exact and highly repetitive.
why_digital: Drawings in, bar lists out to the fabricator's own shop, bought with regional supply.

why_ai: On-site scanning keeps some physical work, while point-cloud modelling is automating fast.
why_clarity: Model accuracy against the scan is measurable and the workflow repeats.
why_digital: Physical buildings scanned on site, modelled remotely, delivered as digital models.

why_ai: Contractual responsibility for coordinated submittals and site conditions keeps accountable people in review.
why_clarity: Review is repetitive, but whether it caught everything shows only in construction.
why_digital: Models and submittals reviewed on screen, tied to physical projects.

why_ai: Statutory authority to object stays with the Office even as form checks automate.
why_clarity: Rule 1.84 form checks are exact and repetitive.
why_digital: Electronic filings reviewed on screen, entirely remote.

why_ai: Software product work that AI tooling accelerates, protected mainly by installed base.
why_clarity: Releases and content are specified and tested against defined requirements.
why_digital: Software sold and delivered online.

why_ai: Labour-arbitrage production is the work AI drawing automation targets first.
why_clarity: Repetitive production against client standards with client acceptance checks.
why_digital: Remote delivery centres serving clients abroad.

why_ai: Analyst reputation and buyer relationships carry the product more than the analysis does.
why_clarity: Provider ratings follow published frameworks, but their correctness is never checked.
why_digital: Briefings and surveys in, reports out, sold internationally.

why_ai: Certification authority and member community give some durability; exam content automates.
why_clarity: Certification standards are defined, but their effect on drawing quality is unmeasured.
why_digital: Exams and guidance online, with conferences in person.

why_ai: Consensus standards carry authority that software cannot replace, though drafting them automates.
why_clarity: Specifications are written by committee and their effect shows over editions.
why_digital: Standards developed and published online through largely remote committees.

why_ai: Matching buyers and drafters is software work and AI may shrink the jobs listed.
why_clarity: Transactions recur in huge numbers with ratings as quick feedback.
why_digital: Fully online marketplaces with a global supply of drafters.

why_ai: Product software built with AI that larger platforms can replicate.
why_clarity: Output quality is testable per sheet, though methods are still evolving.
why_digital: Software sold and delivered online.

why_ai: Pricing rare detailing claims needs accountable underwriting judgement under regulation.
why_clarity: Claims emerge long after policies are written, so pricing feedback is slow.
why_digital: Claims and submissions analysed on screen, policies sold through brokers.

why_ai: Rate guides are content marketing that AI already writes.
why_clarity: Rates are numbers, but definitions of a sheet or ton differ by source.
why_digital: Published online and read by buyers worldwide.
